Alex — thanks for the clear summary. High-level guidance up front: for production-grade, minimum-blast-radius, low-latency connections we typically recommend PrivateLink (interface endpoints) for customer-to-Redwood control/data channels when you need strong cross-account isolation and security. Peering works for simple L3 connectivity inside the same cloud account/region and can be lower cost for large egress volumes, but it exposes broader route visibility and requires careful CIDR planning. Site-to-site VPN is the fastest path for proofs-of-concept (low friction) but has higher operational overhead and can add jitter/latency at scale.

Quick tradeoffs (summary):
- Latency: Peering ~ lowest, PrivateLink ~ slightly higher (ENI hop + proxy), VPN ~ highest and most variable. For p99 150ms target, both peering and PrivateLink are fine if architected correctly; VPN adds risk at high burst.
- Security/isolation: PrivateLink > Peering > VPN (assuming VPN terminates to public IPs or shared VPN appliances). PrivateLink avoids route propagation into your VPC and limits access to specific interface endpoints.
- Routing complexity: Peering requires non-overlapping CIDRs and route propagation; PrivateLink minimal route entries (ENIs), VPN requires tunnels and monitoring.
- Cross-account: PrivateLink is built for cross-account service access without sharing VPC routes; peering is cross-account but requires accept and careful route policies.
- Cost: VPN lowest infra setup cost initially; PrivateLink has per-ENI and per-GB charges; peering has data transfer costs that can be cheaper or more expensive depending on egress patterns.

Recommended phased approach:
1) PoC: Site-to-site VPN to validate traffic patterns and apps (2–4 weeks). Low lead time, lets your app teams run realistic load tests.
2) Prod: PrivateLink for ingress (interface endpoints) as the default for security-sensitive workloads. Add peering only if very large sustained egress makes PrivateLink costs prohibitive and if you can guarantee CIDR non-overlap.

I've attached a short one-pager and a simple matrix I use to walk customers through this (privatelink_vs_peering_onepager.pdf, connectivity_matrix_v1.xlsx). Also flagged a few operational items below you'll want to check:
- Do you have public IPs for VPN termination or will you use an existing transit gateway?
- CIDR plan: avoid 10.0.0.0/8 overlaps with our demo accounts (we can provide our VPC ranges).
- Certificate/KMS requirements for mutual TLS on control channels.

If you're open, let's schedule a short Tech Design Review with NetOps + Security next week — I'll bring Kimberly (implementation) and Marissa (commercial) to answer cost/contract questions.

Alex — following up after our internal sync. Short, pragmatic recommendation and next steps so your Security and NetOps can move forward: 

Recommendation (concise):
- Short-term PoC (0–4 weeks): deploy an IPsec site-to-site VPN between an Acme edge device and your Redwood Private transit endpoint. This validates application behavior under realistic load and requires minimal changes to your CIDR plan.
- Production (4–10 weeks): implement PrivateLink (AWS interface endpoints) in each production VPC/region. PrivateLink provides the strongest isolation, reduces route blast radius, and simplifies least-privilege access for service endpoints.
- Fallback: use VPC peering only if (a) you control CIDR ranges across accounts, and (b) sustained egress cost for PrivateLink becomes materially higher than peering. Peering increases lateral network visibility and operational coupling.

Operational checklist for Acme (items you can share with NetOps):
1) Confirm non-overlapping CIDRs or agree to NAT for specific subranges.
2) Decide where VPN will terminate for the PoC (public IP or transit gateway).
3) Confirm TLS certificate model (we can support mutual TLS on the control channel).
4) Provide expected sustained/peak bandwidth and monthly egress estimate (we used 5TB/mo for pricing).
5) Schedule a 45-minute Tech Design Review — propose Tue 24 Feb 09:00 PT or Wed 25 Feb 14:00 PT.

Commercial notes (Marissa): we'll include typical PrivateLink pricing and a migration discount if Acme commits to Dedicated capacity within 90 days.
